hypothesis: Bounding the local multi-timescale writer's conditional corrective feedback prevents the DEV-034 numerical failure and improves usable prediction and physical decisions compared with the otherwise identical unbounded writer
parameter_and_state_budget: New and unbounded arms have identical trainable initial tensors, parameter count, 768 recurrent scalars and public entity addressing; runtime may differ
bounded_writer: key = raw_key/max(1, norm(raw_key)); alpha is unchanged; beta_effective = alpha*sigmoid(existing_beta_logits); other equations unchanged
conditional_operator: For fixed responsibility, each rank3 value-coordinate row has A=alpha*I-beta_effective*r*k*k^T with eigenvalues alpha and alpha-beta_effective*r*norm(k)^2 in [0,alpha]; full responsibility-coupled Jacobian is not bounded by this statement

training.clipping: dense CPU FP32 gradients, FP64 norm, 1.0; applied to both trained arms
training.failed_arm_handling: save pre-update model, optimizer, RNG, attempted update and exception; never impute a score

selection: No tuning or model selection on the new holdout. Prior archived references are evaluated on the same new cases; one initialization per trained arm, so no architecture superiority claim.
audit: Separate-process exact checkpoint/evaluator replay, split census and independently reconstructed physical outcomes; shared prediction code is not an independent implementation
success_interpretation: Numerical completion and conditional gain bounds are engineering criteria; useful-learning evidence requires improved held-out prediction and cost without over-servicing. One pilot never establishes fresh-seed reliability or complete TAC-OSM capability.
time_budget: Approximately 30 minutes CPU for first research batch; preserve completed evidence if the budget interrupts remaining arms
scope: MTSK memory writer only. No learned identity discovery, action teacher, causal OSM or full-system integration in this experiment. Those are scheduled separately.
